clue.text: Drunkard eating cheese unknown? Not what he's known for

indicators.note: the drunkard consumes the cheese, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
Brie is a soft French cheese
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z, so Y stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: A drunk munching cheese is doing something nobody would expect of him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: a drunkard is famous for the very opposite of this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying sober is precisely the trait a habitual drinker lacks, so it is what he is not known for.

clue.text: Second round — well average

parts.note: O is round in shape
'well' and 'so' both open a remark, as in 'So, what now?'

explanation.surface: A boxer's second round of the fight was merely middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre or middling is described as neither good nor bad, an informal hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Wasn't horrible around relatives

indicators.note: the letters are turned around and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wasn't nasty while in the company of family.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses' brothers are in-laws, members of the family acquired through marriage.

clue.text: Destroyed copter after moving inert military plane

indicators.note: the reworked copter comes after the reworked inert
letters on the move shift into a new order
the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A helicopter was shot down after a stationary aircraft was moved.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast fighter aircraft designed to meet and attack incoming enemy bombers.

clue.text: Sweet time not working middle of week

parts.note: a machine that is off is not running

indicators.note: the centre letters of week are taken

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word week

explanation.surface: Midweek is a period with no work and a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection made by boiling sugar and butter, a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Old friend's a gem

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend

explanation.surface: An old friend is described fondly as a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky iridescent mineral is a precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Friendly about song contest but abandoning EU for now

indicators.note: the friendly word goes around the rest

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

indicators.note: the song contest drops the letters EU

parts.note: Eurovision is the annual European televised song contest
taken as written, the European Union

explanation.surface: A cordial attitude to Eurovision, despite leaving the European Union, sounds like a Brexit-era aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged on a temporary basis, pending confirmation, holds good for the moment only.

clue.text: Record about new worker fully written out

indicators.note: the record goes around the letter for new

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of a voyage
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A record about a new employee is written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary handwriting with words written in full, as opposed to shorthand or abbreviation.

clue.text: Small bird's run quickly

parts.note: the coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: A little bird has dashed off in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart or dash off at speed is an informal verb for going quickly.

clue.text: Decoration one's oft put around

indicators.note: the letters are put around in a different order

explanation.surface: A garland is a decoration that people often hang around a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of flowers or ribbons hung in a curve is an ornamental garland.

clue.text: Actor with an interest to become established in short series

indicators.note: the phrase sits inside the shortened series
the word is cut down to its abbreviation

parts.note: SER is a standard short form of series
to take hold is to become firmly established

explanation.surface: An actor keen to make a name for themselves in a brief TV run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' here means anyone who acts, not a performer: a party with a stake in an enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or group with a stake or concern in a business or project, a party with an interest.

clue.text: What could be hot and horrid ashes all over the place

indicators.note: the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hot fire leaves horrible ashes scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent root is made into a fiery condiment, so it is an example of something hot to taste.

clue.text: As a print reproduced on one side

indicators.note: the letters are copied out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A printed image is copied onto one face of a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan supporter is biased, firmly taking one faction's part.

clue.text: Acknowledged a deadly sin

parts.note: taken as written
greed (avarice) is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone admitted to committing one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: To have accepted or conceded a point is to have consented to it.

clue.text: Be condescending about son's plan

indicators.note: the condescending word wraps around the son

parts.note: to deign is to stoop to do something beneath one

explanation.surface: A parent is patronising about their son's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or intention can be called a design, as in 'by design'.

clue.text: Greatly respect vicar before?

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A parishioner asks whether the vicar deserves deep respect first.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate or hold in awe is to regard with deep admiration.

clue.text: Something in the air, perhaps whistled not badly

indicators.note: something done badly is mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tune whistled quite well is floating in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The fluffy seed heads of a thistle drift on the breeze, an example of something airborne.

clue.text: One changing fabrics in launderette machine — not right

indicators.note: the letter for right is left out

parts.note: a tumble dryer is found in a launderette

explanation.surface: A machine at the launderette is misbehaving and ruining clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who colours cloth alters the appearance of textiles.

clue.text: Rush suddenly around place to spend lavishly

indicators.note: the rush goes around the abbreviation for place

parts.note: a surge is a sudden powerful rush forward

explanation.surface: Shoppers dash to a store to spend extravagantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out or go on a spree means to throw money around.

clue.text: Hang around with daughter and partner

parts.note: an ally is a partner in a cause

explanation.surface: Someone loiters with their daughter and spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or loiter is to waste time idly.

clue.text: Four points for the bulletin?

wordplay.note: the four compass points are north, east, west and south

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks what four key items make up a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast report of current events is the item heard at the top of the hour.

clue.text: One who may sell you ale without something to carry it

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the beer surrounds the tray

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
drinks are carried on a tray

explanation.surface: A barman sells you ale without anything to bring it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, an old sense, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor sells out a friend, so 'sell' here is the idiom for betraying.
